# Fourth Recess Lake (from Mosquito Flat over Mono Pass): research and score

**Score: 77/100.** Scenery 30, Experience 22, Access 13, Permit 12.

It lands just below Lamarck Lakes (79) and Thousand Island Lake (81). It's a better basecamp than Lamarck, with a very good layover-day lineup. It loses points for three things: about 6.5 miles each way with a 12,000-ft pass in both directions, a group of 12 needing every one of the 12 spots released 6 months out, and campsites that get crowded.

## Key facts

| Item | Best figure | Range across sources and notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trailhead | Mosquito Flat, about 10,230 ft | 10,220 (americansouthwest), 10,232 (trailtopeak GPS) |
| Mono Pass | about 12,050 ft | 12,040 (Forest Service flyer), 12,050, 12,060 (hikingwalking) |
| One-way miles to camp | **about 6.5 mi** | 6.03 (AllTrails GPS recording), 6.5 (guidebook cited by 100peaks), about 7.3 if you add up flyfishingthesierra's segments, 8 (Komoot says 16 round trip) |
| Gain on the way in | **about 2,000–2,100 ft** (then about 1,900 ft of descent) | 2,073 (AllTrails recording); "about 2,000 ft each way" (100peaks) |
| Gain on the way out | about 1,950 ft, all of it between 10,100 and 12,050 ft | Komoot gives about 3,935 ft for the round trip, which matches |
| Camp elevation | **about 10,138 ft** | 10,125 (flyfishingthesierra), 10,138 (Mapcarta and AllTrails: 3,090 m), 10,154 (The Dyrt) |
| Coordinates | Longitude −118.7854 (Mapcarta). The north end of the lakeshore trail starts at **37.4437, −118.7865** (Trailforks) | My estimate for the lake's center is about **37.439, −118.785**. I worked that out because the lake runs about 0.9 km north–south. Check it on a USGS map. |
| Lake | About 30 acres, about 0.5 mi long | Granite cliffs and a waterfall at the head of the canyon that 100peaks puts at about 750 ft |

**Which figures I trust:** about 3.7–3.9 miles to the pass. AllTrails contradicts itself on this, saying both "about 3.3" and "just over 4." From the pass, flyfishingthesierra gives about 2.5 miles down to the Fourth Recess junction, and Hiking Project and Calitrails both put the lake 0.5 mile or less up from the junction. I'd plan on **6.5 miles and about 2,000 ft in each direction**. I treat Komoot's 16 miles as a high outlier.

**Land-management detail:** Mapcarta and AllTrails place the lake in Fresno County, on the west side of the crest. I believe that's the Sierra National Forest part of the John Muir Wilderness, but I didn't confirm it with an agency. Either way, the permit you need is Inyo's, because the trip enters from Rock Creek.

## Permit system (from Inyo National Forest and recreation.gov)

- **Entry point name:** "Mono Pass (JMT) (Rock Creek)", code **JM08**. "JMT" here only means the trail connects to the John Muir Trail. Don't confuse it with the Mono Pass near Yosemite.
- **Daily quota:** 20 people. **12 open 6 months ahead**, and **8 are added 2 weeks ahead**, on the same weekday as the entry date. The quota season runs May 1 to Nov 1.
- **Opening time:** reservations open daily at **7:00 AM Pacific**, on a rolling basis. There's **no lottery** (Inyo only runs one for Mt. Whitney). Example: for a Wednesday, July 14, 2027 entry, the 12 advance spots open **Thursday, Jan 14, 2027**. The other 8 open **Wednesday, June 30, 2027**.
- **Group size:** 15 maximum, and that includes day use. Groups can't combine to go over 15, so two permits of 6 are fine.
- **Other rules:**
  - The group must start on the date and at the entry point shown on the permit.
  - The leader and alternate can't be changed.
  - You must print the permit by 10 AM on the entry date or it's canceled. You can print up to 7 days ahead.
  - Fees are $6 per reservation plus $5 per person. That's $66 for one permit of 12.
  - You can change the entry date online only 12 or more days before the trip.
- **Booking URL:** https://www.recreation.gov/permits/233262
- **What this means for 12 people:** you have to get all 12 advance spots in the first minutes at 7:00 AM. If anyone else books even one spot first, your fallback is to split the group. One permit would be booked at the 6-month opening and the other at the 2-week release, which is risky.
  - Little Lakes Valley (JM09, 25 per day, 15 advance) starts at the same trailhead. It's a different entry trail, though, so **ask the Inyo permit office (760-873-2526) before relying on it**.
  - One sign that demand isn't extreme: 100peaks got a permit for two people at the 2-week release in August 2022.

## Fires, closures and access

- **Rock Fire (July 2026):** 12,008 acres, now 100% contained, near Big Pine and Aberdeen. Its closure order runs through Dec 31, 2026 and covers the Sawmill, Red Lake, Taboose and Birch Lake trails. It's well south of Rock Creek and **doesn't affect this route**. The Cinder Complex fire is in the same southern area.
- **Rock Creek Road** is closed from the pack station to Mosquito Flat on **Oct 19–23, 2026** for maintenance. That doesn't matter for a summer trip.
- **Rules:**
  - The Forest Service trail page says no campfires above 10,000 ft. Hiking Project says no campfires at the lake. Plan on stoves only.
  - Bear canisters are required between the trailhead and Mono Pass, and they're the only practical option past the pass.
- **Trailhead:** the road is paved to the trailhead at about 10,230 ft. The parking lot fills up, and some trip reports mention using overflow parking down the road. The Mosquito Flat backpacker campground is one-night-only, which works for acclimatizing the night before. Going from 10,200 to 12,000 ft on the first day is a real altitude-sickness risk for some of the group.
- **Not verified:** the north side of the pass may hold snow early in big snow years. I didn't find a source for 2026 trail conditions.

## How I scored it

- **Scenery 30/35:** The lake sits in a steep granite cirque with a waterfall at the head and Mono Rock above it. The hike in passes Ruby Lake, which the Forest Service describes as emerald water under sheer granite walls, plus Summit Lake and the Trail Lakes, with views of the Recesses and Pioneer Basin from the pass. It's spectacular, but it isn't as famous as the Banner and Ritter views at Thousand Island Lake. The lower end of the lake is forested, and no source I found describes turquoise water.
- **Experience 22/25:** This is an excellent basecamp.
  - **Day hikes:** Dave's Sierra Fishing puts Pioneer Basin's lowest lake 1.5 miles away and its largest lake 3 miles away and 1,000 ft up. A High Sierra Topix poster calls a camp at one of those lakes "arguably one of our finest locations in the range." Third Recess Lake, Snow Lakes and Golden Lake are other options, and peak-baggers can scramble Mono Rock.
  - **Fishing:** sources report rainbows and brookies in the lake (easy catches, mostly small), goldens in Golden Creek and Third Recess, and trout eaten for dinner.
  - **Swimming:** cold, but trip reports describe good swimming.
  - **Campsites (why it isn't higher):** sites are on both sides of the lake, and one report mentions a "huge" site. But Hiking Project says the lake gets crowded in mid-to-late summer, so 12 people may need two neighboring sites.
- **Access 13/20:** About 1 mile longer than your 5.5-mile upper end. The gain is near your past maximum, and you climb about 1,950 ft back to 12,050 ft on the way out. The paved road and high trailhead help.
- **Permit 12/20:** All 12 spots released 6 months ahead are needed for one group of 12. That's better than Lamarck structurally, since its whole daily quota is only 10. It's an all-or-nothing booking at 7:00 AM.
